rationale: Both documents identify the holding component as the white-bear (think/don't-think) construction from the reading-list paper (papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering), explicitly stating it is used as a known, calibrated component rather than as the method itself, and both frame the read-mode component and the holding+read-mode composite as the novel contribution. The numerical results differ only in rounding precision (0.61/0.78/0.13-0.17 vs 0.608/0.784/0.167), which is not a material difference in sourcing, overlap, or novelty framing, so the two documents agree on the source and its treatment.
